# Releases

Push a new version tag such as `v0.1.0` or `v0.1.0-rc.1` on the reviewed commit. The tag-triggered Release workflow runs the full CI workflow, creates or resumes a draft release, and builds the shared Dockerfile for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`.

The workflow publishes the versioned GHCR image, attaches the installation archive and SHA-256 checksum, and verifies a pull of the exact image digest. Public repositories require anonymous access; private repositories use the authenticated workflow identity and retain private package visibility. Only then does it publish the GitHub Release. Tags with a prerelease suffix produce prereleases and are excluded from the README's latest stable download URL. A failed build, upload, or pull leaves the release unpublished; rerun the failed workflow after resolving the cause. Published versions are not overwritten.

New GHCR packages are private by default. While the repository is private, keep its package private and grant installation users read access to both the repository and the package. When making the repository public, also set the GHCR package visibility to **Public** in its package settings; the two visibility settings are separate. Public releases must pass the anonymous-access gate. The workflow's registry login does not prove users can pull without credentials. See [GitHub's Container registry documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/packages/working-with-a-github-packages-registry/working-with-the-container-registry).

The archive contains the shared Compose deployment, configuration initializer, release updater, README, runtime example, and `release.env` with the image digest. Installation and release updates require no source checkout, Node.js installation, npm, or local build. Release notes must state storage compatibility: an existing installation must match the candidate's exact schema or use a separately verified clean restore. Image replacement is not a schema upgrade.

The deployment guide covers fresh installation, configuration, and updates through `deploy/deploy.sh --update [TAG]`. Without a tag it selects the latest stable release; interrupted recovery resumes the recorded candidate. Operators using a source checkout retain the no-argument build-and-update path. Both use the same authority verification and recovery fence. GitHub CLI's [draft release controls](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_release_create) keep installation assets out of public release discovery until publication.
